segments.say: Lesson 14. Lang Chain Essentials. Models, prompts, output parsers, retrievers and L C E L pipes: the building blocks, with code.

Lang Chain is a Python/J S framework that gives standard building blocks (model wrappers, prompt templates, retrievers, tools, parsers) and a pipe syntax to connect them into L L M apps. Here is an analogy. L E G O Technic for L L M apps: standard pieces with matching connectors, so swapping one model or vector store for another doesn't mean rebuilding everything.

Why does this matter? Widely used in industry and named in many A I job descriptions. Lang Graph and Lang Smith build on its interfaces. A few key words. Runnable: Any Lang Chain component with invoke/stream/batch. L C E L: The pipe syntax: prompt model parser. Retriever: Component that returns relevant documents. Output parser: Turns model text into strings, jason or objects.

segments.say: An L C E L chain: prompt model parser. Lang Chain gives you Runnables: components with the same interface ( invoke, batch, stream, ainvoke ).

segments.say: Chained with the pipe: chain equals prompt llm parser. That's L C E L (Lang Chain Expression Language), and you get streaming, batching and tracing for free.

Core building blocks. Chat models: ChatAnthropic, ChatOpenAI. with.bind tools() and.with structured output(). Prompts: ChatPromptTemplate.from messages(. ), plus MessagesPlaceholder for history. Document loaders & text splitters: RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter. Embeddings & vector stores: PGVector, Chroma, F A I S S, Pinecone, then.as retriever(search kwargs= "k":4 ). Output parsers: StrOutputParser, JsonOutputParser, PydanticOutputParser. Tools: the @tool decorator turns a Python function into a tool schema.

A minimal rag chain (Python). from langchain core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
from langchain core.output parsers import StrOutputParser
from langchain core.runnables import RunnablePassthrough prompt equals ChatPromptTemplate.from messages( ("system", "Answer only from the context. Cite sources.\n<context> context </context>"), ("human", " question ") ) chain equals ( "context": retriever format docs, "question": RunnablePassthrough() prompt llm StrOutputParser()) chain.invoke("How do I rotate the A P I key?")

Lang Chain versus Lang Graph. Lang Chain gives you the components and simple linear chains. When you need loops, branching, state, retries, human approval or multi-agent flows, use Lang Graph (next lesson). Today, Lang Chain agents are built on Lang Graph under the hood.

Interview honesty. Know the common criticisms: too much abstraction, fast-moving A P Is, and hard debugging without tracing. Good answer: "I use Lang Chain for integrations and standard interfaces, keep business logic in plain Python, and trace everything in Lang Smith.".

Say it in the interview. "Lang Chain standardizes models, prompts, retrievers, tools and parsers behind the Runnable interface. L C E L composes them with pipes and gives me streaming, batching, async and tracing. For anything stateful or cyclic I move to Lang Graph.".

Let's compare. Swap L L M vendors: Chat model integrations. Reusable prompts with variables: ChatPromptTemplate. Guaranteed jason / Pydantic: with structured output. Search your docs: VectorStore.as retriever(). Expose a Python function to the L L M: @tool plus bind tools. Compose steps: L C E L pipe, RunnableParallel, RunnablePassthrough. Loops, state, human approval: leads to Lang Graph.

A likely interview question: Why use Lang Chain at all? A strong answer: Standard interfaces across many providers and integrations (models, vector stores, loaders, tools), composition with L C E L, and built-in streaming, batching and async plus Lang Smith tracing. Keep core logic in plain Python to limit lock-in.
That's it for Lang Chain Essentials. Now play the quiz and games in the app to lock it in. See you in the next lesson.
